accepted.s: India has approximately how many languages listed in UNESCO’s Atlas of Endangered Languages?
accepted.x: India has about 197 languages listed in UNESCO’s Atlas of Endangered Languages, the highest number for any country.
accepted.tq: Use the precise numerical figure and eliminate nearby altered values.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Scheme for Protection and Preservation of Endangered Languages (SPPEL) was launched in which year?
accepted.x: SPPEL is a Union Education Ministry scheme introduced in 2013.
accepted.tq: Test the year of a named government scheme directly.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: SPPEL is implemented by which institution?
o: National Council of Educational Research and Training, New Delhi
Tribal Research and Training Institute, Bhubaneswar
Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysuru
accepted.x: SPPEL is run by the Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL), Mysuru.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘which institution implements it?’ trap among neighbouring language bodies.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: SPPEL primarily covers languages having fewer than:
accepted.x: SPPEL is intended for the protection and preservation of languages with fewer than 10,000 speakers.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the scheme’s eligibility threshold from nearby figures.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which State published a comprehensive bilingual tribal dictionary series for preserving vanishing tribal languages?
accepted.x: Odisha published a comprehensive bilingual tribal dictionary series for preserving vanishing tribal languages.
accepted.tq: Use the location-based trap by matching the preservation measure with the correct State.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding tribal-language preservation in Odisha:
1. Odisha runs multilingual education in 21 tribal languages.
2. The programme covers 1,483 schools.
3. The schools are spread across 17 districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: Odisha’s multilingual education programme covers 21 tribal languages, 1,483 schools and 17 districts.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical component separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The endangered tribal languages Mavila and Malaveduvan are associated with which region?
accepted.x: Mavila and Malaveduvan are endangered tribal languages of the Kannur-Kasaragod region of northern Kerala.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related regional locations.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The dictionaries prepared for Mavila and Malaveduvan reportedly contain more than:
accepted.x: The dictionaries document more than 5,000 words of the Mavila and Malaveduvan languages.
accepted.tq: Test a quantitative detail using graduated distractor values.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a threat to endangered tribal languages?
o: Availability of scripts for tribal languages
Dominance of English on the internet
Absence of schooling in the mother tongue
accepted.x: Availability of scripts is not a threat; rather, the lack of scripts for tribal languages is identified as a threat. Migration, nuclear families, English dominance and lack of mother-tongue schooling are threats.
accepted.tq: Find the single reversed or negative formulation among otherwise valid threats.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bhasha Sangam, launched in 2018, was associated with which initiative?
accepted.x: Bhasha Sangam was a 2018 initiative under Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat.
accepted.tq: Match a named initiative with its parent programme and year.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The primary objective of Bhasha Sangam for school students was to enable them to learn simple sentences in:
accepted.x: Bhasha Sangam encouraged school students to learn simple sentences in all 22 scheduled languages.
accepted.tq: Separate a constitutional language count from other language classifications.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the languages cited in connection with the Adi Vaani platform?
accepted.x: Adi Vaani is associated with Bhili, Gondi, Mundari and Santhali; Koya is not included in the listed group.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘not included’ format to test membership in a named list.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy’s contribution to the Savara language included:
1. Designing a script for Savara.
2. Preparing Savara-Telugu dictionaries.
3. Preparing a Savara manual.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Gidugu designed a script for Savara and prepared both Savara-Telugu dictionaries and a Savara manual.
accepted.tq: Combine several related contributions and verify each item before choosing the code.
accepted.sec: Endangered languages - UNESCO list, SPPEL scheme, tribal dictionaries  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Official Language Act declaring Telugu as the official language of Andhra Pradesh was enacted in:
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Official Language Act was enacted in 1966 and declared Telugu the official language of the State.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original Act from a later amendment.
accepted.sec: Official languages of AP - AP Official Language Act, second official language, Telugu status  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Official Language (Amendment) Act, 2022 is associated with which development?
o: Making Urdu the second official language statewide
Recognition of Telugu as a classical language
Creation of the Telugu Language Commission
Moving the Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Telugu to Nellore
accepted.x: The 2022 amendment made Urdu the second official language of Andhra Pradesh throughout the State.
accepted.tq: Separate the original enactment from the later amendment and its specific effect.
accepted.sec: Official languages of AP - AP Official Language Act, second official language, Telugu status  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Telugu is correct?
1. It belongs to the Dravidian language family.
2. It has been a classical language since 2008.
3. It is included among the 22 scheduled languages.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Telugu is a Dravidian language, is one of the 22 scheduled languages and was recognised as a classical language in 2008.
accepted.tq: Use a coded combination to test classification, constitutional listing and status together.
accepted.sec: Official languages of AP - AP Official Language Act, second official language, Telugu status  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Telugu, a wing of CIIL, was moved to:
accepted.x: The Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Telugu was moved to Nellore.
accepted.tq: Test the headquarters or relocation site directly.
accepted.sec: Official languages of AP - AP Official Language Act, second official language, Telugu status  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who is the president of the Mandali Venkata Krishna Rao Official Language Commission of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: P. Trivikram Rao is the president of the Mandali Venkata Krishna Rao Official Language Commission.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the commission’s namesake from its current president.
accepted.sec: Official languages of AP - AP Official Language Act, second official language, Telugu status  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August to commemorate the birth anniversary of:
accepted.x: Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August, the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy.
accepted.tq: Link the commemorative date with the correct personality rather than the language movement generally.
accepted.sec: Official languages of AP - AP Official Language Act, second official language, Telugu status  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy is especially associated with which movement?
accepted.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy is regarded as the father of the Vyavaharika, or colloquial, Telugu movement.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related descriptions of a language reform movement.
accepted.sec: Official languages of AP - AP Official Language Act, second official language, Telugu status  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The earliest Telugu word ‘Nagabu’ is found in the:
accepted.x: The earliest Telugu word, ‘Nagabu’, is recorded in an Amaravati inscription.
accepted.tq: Match the earliest linguistic evidence with its inscriptional location.
accepted.sec: Official languages of AP - AP Official Language Act, second official language, Telugu status  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which inscription is regarded as the first fully Telugu inscription?
accepted.x: The Kalamalla inscription of 575 CE, associated with the Renati Cholas of Kadapa, is regarded as the first fully Telugu inscription.
accepted.tq: Use the distinction between the earliest Telugu word and the first fully Telugu inscription.
accepted.sec: Official languages of AP - AP Official Language Act, second official language, Telugu status  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Telugu is popularly known as the:
accepted.x: Telugu is popularly called the ‘Italian of the East’.
accepted.tq: Test a well-known sobriquet using close but incorrect cultural comparisons as distractors.

accepted.s: Which Telugu dialect region is regarded as the base of standard Telugu?
o: Coastal Andhra, particularly the Krishna-Godavari region
accepted.x: The Coastal dialect region, especially the Krishna-Godavari area, is regarded as the base of standard Telugu.
accepted.tq: Match the dialect region with its linguistic significance.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct set of major Telugu dialect regions mentioned for Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The major regions are Coastal, Rayalaseema, Kalinga/Uttarandhra and Telangana.
accepted.tq: Select the complete geographical classification while rejecting an inserted unrelated region.

accepted.x: Savara, also known as Sora, is associated with the Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills and is noted for rich folk literature.
accepted.tq: Use a location-and-cultural-feature combination to identify the language.

accepted.s: Kui/Kuvi, also known as Kondh, is spoken mainly in the:
accepted.x: Kui/Kuvi is associated with the hills along the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border.
accepted.tq: Test the border-region association of a tribal language.

accepted.s: Which statement regarding Gadaba is correct?
o: It is an Austro-Asiatic language confined to the Krishna delta.
It is a Dravidian language spoken only in the Godavari agency.
It has Munda Gutob and Dravidian Ollari varieties and is found in the Visakhapatnam-Vizianagaram agency.
It is exclusively an Indo-Aryan language of the Banjaras.
accepted.x: Gadaba includes Munda Gutob and Dravidian Ollari varieties and is associated with the Visakhapatnam-Vizianagaram agency.
accepted.tq: Avoid the exclusive-word trap and distinguish a language with multiple varieties from single-family languages.
accepted.sec: Languages of AP - Telugu dialects, tribal languages, Urdu speakers  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Gor Boli is correct?
1. It is associated with the Lambadi or Banjara community.
2. It belongs to the Indo-Aryan family.
3. It has no native script and may be written in Telugu, Devanagari or Kannada scripts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Gor Boli is an Indo-Aryan language of the Banjara community; it has no native script and is written using Telugu, Devanagari or Kannada scripts.
accepted.tq: Check community, family and script features independently before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Languages of AP - Telugu dialects, tribal languages, Urdu speakers  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The AP State Urdu Academy provides free computer training through how many centres?
accepted.x: The AP State Urdu Academy runs free computer training in 36 centres.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact institutional coverage figure from nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Languages of AP - Telugu dialects, tribal languages, Urdu speakers  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Deccani Urdu developed during the rule of the Qutb Shahis in a context where:
o: Telugu was the official language and Persian was spoken by the people
Urdu was the official language and Sanskrit was spoken by the people
Persian was the official language and Telugu was spoken by the people
Kannada was the official language and Marathi was spoken by the people
accepted.x: Deccani Urdu dates to the Qutb Shahi period, when Persian was the official language and Telugu was spoken by the people.
accepted.tq: Test the reversed relationship between official and popular languages.
